pr_title: Don't skip validation if target is new record
pr_body:
Fixes #54267

/cc @Edouard-chin for working on #54273, I was coming up with a test for this when you pushed :joy: could you check it? :bow:
pr_comments:
I'm not sure how frequent this would be as I can't think of a way to replicate with the nested attribute thing. But manually modifying the relation could still be an issue, this test https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/05e3551877a37663691165572fc04475a025d5d0/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb#L1556 failed with this patch.

If for instance we build a new `liquid` and call `liquid.molecules = existing_molecules`. This would prevent changes made to electrons to being validated.

> If for instance we build a new liquid and call liquid.molecules = existing_molecules. This would prevent changes made to electrons to being validated.

I was able to reproduce it too, here's an example of that case failing with this branch.

```
    1575:     liquid.reload
    1576:
    1577:     new_liquid = Liquid.new
    1578:     molecule.electrons.first.name = ""
 => 1579:     binding.irb
    1580:   end
    1581:
    1582:   def test_a_child_marked_for_destruction_should_not_be_destroyed_twice_while_saving_habtm
    1583:     @pirate.parrots.create!(name: "parrots_1")
    1584:

>> molecule.electrons
=> [#<Electron:0x00007f9ed63beb20 id: 1, molecule_id: 1, name: "">, #<Electron:0x00007f9ed628ba78 id: nil, molecule_id: 1, name: "">]
>> molecule.save
=> false
>> l = Liquid.new
=> #<Liquid:0x00007f9edcb92940 id: nil, name: nil>
>> l.molecules << molecule
=> [#<Molecule:0x00007f9ed62a4168 id: 1, liquid_id: 1, name: nil>]
>> l.save
=> true
```

Should we try to support it for (already persisted) grand children?

IMHO I think yes. Well at least I would expect `new_liquid.molecules = existing_molecules` to behave the same as `existing_liquid.molecules = existing_molecules`.

----- 

I believe the issue with conditionally validating is that we stop the validation chain at some point and subsequent dirty relation would go through without validation. That's why maybe we should validate inconditionally and do some computing (what the PR I open does).

But I don't have strong opinion and your patch is way simpler so I'll let you and other core members decide, happy to close my PR :) !

> But I don't have strong opinion and your patch is way simpler so I'll let you and other core members decide

Thanks so much for your time and reviewing this. I also don't feel strongly about this one, I'm just here to learn and try to help contribute to the framework that gave me so much.

This was a fun issue to dig into over my morning coffee :joy: especially because it has easy to follow repro test case.

Let's wait for a review from Jean or someone who is more confident about the trade-offs here.

👋 Thank you both for hopping on this so quickly! I've verified that @zzak 's changes are enough to fix the regression we were seeing in our CI build at Shopify.

> Should we try to support it for (already persisted) grand children?

Using the test case zzak wrote, AFAICT this would've been a problem prior to the change Jean made:

```ruby
  def test_new_parent_existing_invalid_grandchildren
    liquid = Liquid.new
    molecule = liquid.molecules.build

    liquid.save!

    input_attributes = {
      molecules_attributes: {
        "0" => {
          id: molecule.id,
          electrons_attributes: { id: nil, name: "" }
        }
      }
    }
    refute liquid.update(input_attributes)

    liquid.reload

    molecule.electrons.first.name = ""
    refute molecule.save

    new_liquid = Liquid.new
    new_liquid.molecules = liquid.molecules

    refute new_liquid.save, "Liquid should not have been saved"
  end
```

(This fails prior to 67497678b9679be32ca02682e35239b9cd50573d, and on this branch).

So perhaps that could be addressed separately, with this PR addressing the true "regression" introduced in https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54267, as demonstrated by the regression test you wrote, zzak?

👋 Hey Adrianna !

FWIW, the test case you added has a small mistake. (calling liquid.molecules reload the relation from the DB and discard the changes we have just made to the electron).


```diff
diff --git a/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb b/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
index 13f4cac7fc..29b9c2d933 100644
--- a/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
+++ b/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
@@ -1575,10 +1575,10 @@ def test_new_parent_existing_invalid_grandchildren

     new_liquid = Liquid.new
-    new_liquid.molecules = liquid.molecules
+    new_liquid.molecules = [molecule]

-    refute liquid.save, "Liquid should not have been saved"
+    refute new_liquid.save, "Liquid should not have been saved"
   end

   def test_a_child_marked_for_destruction_should_not_be_destroyed_twice_while_saving_habtm
```

This works (it validates the electron) prior to https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/67497678b9679be32ca02682e35239b9cd50573d

Hey @Edouard-chin, nice to see you again 😄 Arf, I must not have had my coffee yet when I wrote that test case 🤦‍♀️ Indeed, what I meant to do (following zzak's repro in IRB) was
```diff
diff --git a/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb b/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
index 7f95036d1b..0a5f7fe099 100644
--- a/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
+++ b/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
@@ -1595,7 +1595,7 @@ def test_foo
     refute molecule.save
 
     new_liquid = Liquid.new
-    new_liquid.molecules = liquid.molecules
+    new_liquid.molecules << molecule
 
     refute new_liquid.save, "Liquid should not have been saved"
```
which does pass prior to https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53951/commits/67497678b9679be32ca02682e35239b9cd50573d, as with the example you provided.

So perhaps we'd like to verify whether anything in the association chain has changed and is invalid...

Ok, just so we're all on the same page I committed the failing test in a74361826981b8d2200331f14595319dbe285499 which does _not_ fail on #54273 or prior to 6749767.

Due to that, I think we should consider Edouardo's PR or possibly reverting it, but there was a lot more changes and discussion in #18612 so it needs some more careful investigation.

I don't think this change is enough so I'm going to close it, thank you both for taking a look and feel free to re-use the test cases in another PR.

issue_context.title: [Regression] Invalid doubly-nested attributes are saved
issue_context.body:
I believe https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53951 introduced a regression into saving nested attributes if there is more than one level of nesting. Repro:

```ruby
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", ref: "9424179306" # commit prior to change

  gem "sqlite3"

  gem "debug"
end

require "active_record/railtie"
require "minitest/autorun"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :countries do |t|
    t.string :name
  end

  create_table :tax_overrides do |t|
    t.string :name
    t.references :country
  end

  create_table :tax_override_regions do |t|
    t.string :name
    t.references :tax_override
    t.decimal :rate, precision: 10, scale: 2
  end
end

class Country < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :tax_overrides

  accepts_nested_attributes_for :tax_overrides
end

class TaxOverride < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :country
  has_many :tax_override_regions

  accepts_nested_attributes_for :tax_override_regions
end

class TaxOverrideRegion < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :tax_override

  validates :rate, numericality: { greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }, allow_nil: false
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_validation_issue
    country = Country.build(name: "Canada")
    tax_override = country.tax_overrides.build(name: "Tax Override for Ontario")
    tax_override_region = tax_override.tax_override_regions.build(name: "Toronto", rate: 10.0)

    country.save!

    input_attributes = {
      tax_overrides_attributes:
      {"0" =>
        {
          id: tax_override.id,
          tax_override_regions_attributes: {"0" => { rate: -0.4, id: tax_override_region.id }},
        }
      }
    }

    refute country.update(input_attributes), "Country should not have been updated"
    assert country.errors.full_messages.include?(
      "Tax overrides tax override regions rate must be greater than or equal to 0"
    )
  end
end
```

Before change, the test passes.

On main:
```
  1) Failure:
BugTest#test_validation_issue [scripts/no-validation-bug.rb:73]:
Country should not have been updated

1 runs, 1 assertions, 1 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips
```

cc @byroot

review_comments:
Would this work in case the record is already persisted but we are modifying it with invalid value ?

E.g. in your existing test, if one tries to update an existing electron?

Thanks for taking a look!

I've added a test for this:

```diff
--- a/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
+++ b/activerecord/test/cases/autosave_association_test.rb
@@ -1550,6 +1550,27 @@ def test_should_not_skip_validation_on_deeply_nested_attributes_if_unpersisted_a

     assert_not liquid.update(input_attributes), "Liquid should not have been updated"
     assert_includes liquid.errors.full_messages, "Molecules electrons name can't be blank"
+
+    liquid.reload
+
+    electron = molecule.electrons.build(name: "electron")
+    electron.save!
+
+    assert_predicate liquid, :valid?
+    assert_predicate electron, :persisted?
+    assert_predicate electron, :valid?
+
+    input_attributes = {
+      molecules_attributes: {
+        "0" => {
+          id: molecule.id,
+          electrons_attributes: { id: electron.id, name: "" }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+
+    assert_not liquid.update(input_attributes), "Liquid should not have been updated"
+    assert_includes liquid.errors.full_messages, "Molecules electrons name can't be blank"
   end
```
